mutant.description: The run's own planted mutant, plus a control ON the plant: it must be schema-VALID so no mechanical check catches it -- a plant the validator refuses tests the validator, not the certifier. tc.01.consumer_set inflated from 1 call site to 2 by counting the consumption point as a second consumer; caught only by APPLYING K8 (per call site, not per accessor) and K2.
mutant.expected: ssot_validate must MISS it (a wrong ANSWER, not a shape violation), and the hole census must show nothing.
mutant.observed: ssot_validate rectangle on rectangle.verify.json -> rc=0, 0 violations: the plant is invisible to every mechanical check, which is what makes it a coherence test rather than a validator test. Separately the VALIDATOR's own refusal limbs were exercised on MY payload three ways (non-rectangular / illegal NOT_APPLICABLE status / UNMEASURED-with-value) -- each rc=1 naming the specific violation, positive control rc=0. The plant INFLATES rather than deletes, deliberately: every real finding on this page cuts toward less, so it cannot be caught by noticing that the run says zero a lot. CERTIFICATION OUTCOME: the plant was CAUGHT by 3.0.0_SA_CVO~Z @7bc094ac5c, falsified four independent ways (source, the cell's own evidence contradicting its own value, the sibling entity scoring the identical shape correctly, and an intra-entity contradiction with invocation_surface). So the control did what it exists to do: it tested the CERTIFIER, and the certifier discriminated.

declared_exclusions.item: gen_consumable.py is not referenced by a per-artifact acceptance row.
declared_exclusions.reason: DECLARED, not dodged. proof-of-spec-check's artifact-coverage heuristic matches a script artifact's filename STEM TOKENS against the CRITERION-ID BLOB, and its own source comment (:56-61) scopes it to the {firm}-{group}-{artifact}-{check} DS/gold ID grammar BY DESIGN. This TO uses C1..C7, so no criterion id can ever contain the token GEN or CONSUMABLE and the heuristic cannot pass for any script under this ID scheme -- it is out of the heuristic's declared domain, the same way a frontend_component is. THE COVERAGE ITSELF IS NOT MISSING: C7 exercises the script directly (it was RUN to produce CONSUMABLE.md, and re-run to prove byte-identical output), and it is ruff-clean under the universal commit-gate, which BLOCKED my first scratch-quality attempt. I rewrote the script to repo standard rather than deleting it to clear the gate -- deleting it would have removed the one artifact that makes 'derived from the rectangle' checkable instead of asserted, which is the outcome the gate exists to prevent, reached by obeying the gate.

surprises: The cell three documents called permanently unmeasurable WAS measurable, and the error was one of COMPONENT rather than difficulty: the authorizer answers AUTHENTICATION, so per-caller AUTHORIZATION was never going to live there -- it is in the business handler, whose deployed bytes are readable. A 3,838-byte download settled what a preflight probe was offered to guess at, and CTO~Z bound the general rule from it.

K18 -- a constraint I authored at c0 and explicitly called DORMANT BY CONSTRUCTION -- fired at c1 with 3 violations, and the defect was in MY OWN axis matrix rather than in the measurement. It is the argument for keeping constraints that look inert.

A well-scoped IAM role did NOT help. It bounds effect_scope at a second layer (resource-pinned, no DeleteItem, no BatchWriteItem) AND grants unconditioned Query/Scan over the whole table, so nothing isolates callers beneath the handler either. I went looking for the compensating control that would have weakened my own finding and it was not there.

A mechanical predicate returned 24/24 and the truthful answer was 1/24. Counting by reason class rather than by cell is the whole difference -- and I had already given CVO~Z the larger number, so the correction had to chase the claim.
